punchline: By Robbins's count, 37 runners broke four minutes within a year of Bannister, after thousands of years of 'impossible'.
thirty_sec: Tony Robbins says a belief is a tabletop, and experiences are its legs. For thousands of years people believed nobody could run a mile in under four minutes. In 1954 Roger Bannister did, after rehearsing the run in his mind. Robbins writes that 37 other runners broke four minutes within a year and 300 the year after. His reading: once there was one example, the others had a leg to stand on.
